transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Good morning everyone and welcome to the, um, to the committee. I'd like to start by noting apologies. We have none, I believe. Clerk?

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: No apologies, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Thank you. Item one is the evidence session on rural connectivity, and before that, a short matter of business. Members will recall we agreed last time to look at the draft terms of reference.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Yes, Chair. I had a question on the scope. Are we looking only at fixed broadband?

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: That is exactly what I wanted to settle. Alun?

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Thank you, Chair. My view is that it would be odd to ignore mobile. In many of the valleys people have no signal at all, never mind a fibre cable.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I agree with that. The constituents I speak to mention both in the same breath.

transcript.speaker: Carys Evans
transcript.text: If I may, from the officials' side, we hold data for both so it would not be a problem.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: So is it the view of members that the inquiry should cover both broadband and mobile coverage?

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Yes, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Then it is agreed. The inquiry covers both.

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: I will note that in the minutes.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Thank you. Now, we have heard from the fixed network providers in March. For mobile, I propose we take oral evidence from the operators in June.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: I would support that. The sooner the better.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Chair, if we hear from them in June, would it be, would it not be wise to see the figures first?

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: That is a fair point. Carys, can the officials supply the coverage figures?

transcript.speaker: Carys Evans
transcript.text: We can, Chair. I will provide the coverage figures broken down by local authority. I do not have the final date because we are waiting on the regulator's release, but it will be before the next meeting.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Before the next meeting. Thank you, Carys.

transcript.speaker: Carys Evans
transcript.text: Of course.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Members, are we content to take oral evidence from the operators in June?

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Content.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Content, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Agreed. Clerk, you would then invite the operators.

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: Yes, Chair. I will send the invitations to the operators this week, once we have the dates confirmed with the, uh, with the members' diaries.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, the draft report from the earlier inquiry. Clerk, where are we?

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: The draft is complete, Chair. I will circulate it to members by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: By this Friday. The fifteenth. Good.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: That is helpful, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I wonder if the weather will be like this on Friday. It has not stopped raining since Sunday.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: It is the same in my constituency. The roads are, well, I will not go into it.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Members, if we could stay with the agenda. Now, on the evidence, I wonder whether the minister should be written to.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I would be glad to do that, Chair. There is the matter of the coverage targets that the Government has set, which as far as I can see have not been met in any of the rural areas.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Would you draft the letter, Rhys?

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I will write to the minister about the coverage targets. I would say within a fortnight.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Within a fortnight. So by the twenty-sixth. Good.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Chair, may I suggest, perhaps the committee should visit a village in Powys? To see the problem first hand? I think it would add a lot to the report.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: That is an interesting idea. It would need to be costed and the clerk would need to look at the programme.

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: It would be rather difficult to do in the current budget, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Then we shall hold it as a suggestion and return to it. I do not want to commit members today.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: If we had a bigger budget we could go to every county.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: If we had a bigger budget, Rhys, there would be several other things I would do first.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Quite, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: There is the matter of the licence conditions. If an operator has promised coverage in their licence and has not delivered, is there any legal remedy? I would like to know.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Would you look into that, Alun?

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: I will have a look, Chair. I am not a lawyer so I can promise nothing, but I will try to find out what the position is.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Thank you. Now before the operators come, it would help if somebody met them informally. Who is going to meet the operators beforehand?

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I do not think it is appropriate for a member to do that.

transcript.speaker: Carys Evans
transcript.text: It would not be for the officials either, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: Nor the clerk, Chair, it would be seen as a breach of impartiality.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Hmm. Then it is unresolved. We shall come back to it.

transcript.speaker: Megan Jones
transcript.text: Chair, may I correct myself on the draft report. I said Friday. I think I will need until Monday the eighteenth because the translation unit has not yet returned the Welsh version.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Monday the eighteenth. Very well. Members will have it Monday.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: That is fine, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: I do apologise, Chair, I must leave at noon for another committee.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: That is understood, Rhys. Which one is it?

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: The finance committee, Chair, they are discussing the winter budget.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pritchard
transcript.text: Is there any other business? No. Then I thank members and officials. The committee is adjourned.

transcript.speaker: Rhys Davies
transcript.text: Thank you, Chair.

transcript.speaker: Alun Hughes
transcript.text: Thank you.

decisions.text: The committee will take oral evidence from the mobile operators in June
The inquiry will cover both broadband and mobile coverage
